label: Sabaeans
conclusion: By the 2015 cutoff, general ancient Near Eastern slavery scholarship and accessible South-Arabian epigraphic infrastructure make slavery a plausible regional research category, but this bounded reconstruction does not yet establish a Sabaean slavery/practice claim specifically at c.500 BCE.
abstention: Do not infer Sabaean practice from generic ancient Near Eastern slavery or from ambiguous ʿbd terminology without target-specific contextual interpretation.

sources.title: Slavery in the Ancient Near East
sources.author: Daniel C. Snell

label: Chámpa
conclusion: Pre-2016 scholarship reports early-thirteenth-century descriptions of people being bought and made slaves in Champa, supporting a bounded slavery/slave-purchasing claim near the 1300 anchor.
abstention: Do not infer territorial prevalence across all Champa from commercial/transactional evidence.

sources.title: Money, Markets, and Trade in Early Southeast Asia
sources.author: Robert S. Wicks

label: Alodia
conclusion: A late-sixth-century or later papyrus concerning sale of an Alodian slave girl establishes a bounded later transaction/context, not slavery in Alodia at exactly 500 CE.
abstention: Do not back-project the later slave-sale evidence to the 500 anchor.

sources.title: A sale of an Alodian slave girl
sources.author: Richard Holton Pierce

label: Janapada of Aśmaka
conclusion: Ancient-Indian scholarship available before 2016 documents slavery/servitude in the broader Buddhist-era world but does not establish Aśmaka-specific practice at c.500 BCE.
abstention: Do not transfer broad dāsa/dāsī or regional slavery categories into Aśmaka.

label: Cao
conclusion: Pre-2016 early-China scholarship documents slavery/unfree categories and later legal evidence but does not establish a Cao-specific slavery institution at c.500 BCE.
abstention: Do not treat later Qin legal categories or broad Eastern-Zhou hierarchy as Cao territorial practice.

sources.title: Slavery in Early China: A Socio-Cultural Approach
sources.author: Robin D. S. Yates

label: Janapada of Vatsa
conclusion: Pre-2016 ancient-Indian slavery scholarship establishes slavery/servitude as a regional historical category but does not securely identify Vatsa-specific slavery at c.500 BCE.
abstention: Do not map broad dāsa, Śūdra, or regional servitude evidence directly onto Vatsa.
